# Obsidian Research Notes
Use the research vault `/mnt/c/Users/boren/code/ASR-Research` (unless the user specifies another vault). Inspect applicable vault instructions, current notes, homepage navigation, and Git status before editing; write in the surrounding notes’ language, currently Chinese.

## Inputs from comparison workflows
Use the completed analysis and artifacts supplied by the calling skill; keep note-writing instructions here rather than duplicating them in comparison skills.

- `asr-detail-compare` supplies its summary JSON, ranked HTML reports, source identities, scoring/join details, and reviewed utterance findings. It requests vault deliverables by default unless the user opts out.
- `report-experiment` supplies a verified PDF report, supporting Markdown, plotted data, reusable figures, run identities, step coverage, setting differences, validation and `reward-core` findings, and evidence/limitations. It requests the detailed note and affected daily homepage by default unless the user opts out. Refresh an existing note/entry for the same comparison; retain report dependencies when copying assets. Legacy `compare-asr-experiments` artifacts can supply the same evidence when a note update is requested.
- Produce both the detailed note and affected daily homepage. For experiment comparisons, summarize config/code differences, per-dataset validation, comparable reward means, and matched error patterns where supported. For utterance comparisons, retain the scoring and matching details below. Missing evidence remains a stated gap rather than a requirement to launch new work.

## Detailed research note
- For comparison reports, write the analysis under `06-对比与结论/`, following the existing `对比 · <topic>.md` naming and frontmatter conventions (`type: comparison`, date, and a concise `homepage_summary`). Search for an existing note covering the same dataset, baseline/target run identities, and checkpoint steps before creating one. Update that note for a rerun or corrected analysis; keep distinct comparisons identifiable and preserve relevant historical evidence.
- For ASR comparison notes, include the dataset and exact model/run/step identities, source JSONL paths, scoring/normalization and join key, matched/excluded sample counts and reference consistency, dataset-level WER and error totals, improved/degraded/unchanged counts, and the main findings with a few representative cases. Distinguish full-dataset metrics from ranked top-N examples and retain material comparability limitations. For single-result reviews, describe target errors against reference rather than model improvement.
- Link the available source reports (summary, HTML, PDF, and evidence) using their actual filenames; only link artifacts that exist. Retain the complete report on disk; do not copy all utterance rows into the note. For vault-visible figures or copied report assets, use a stable report-specific directory under `80-资料/实验总结/<comparison>/` and preserve HTML relative dependencies such as `audio/`. Reuse existing assets for the same report.

## Daily homepage
- Update the affected `00-首页/YYYY-MM-DD · 实验对比与分析.md`. Honor an explicit report date or the existing report’s evidence-date convention; otherwise use the reporting day in `America/Los_Angeles`. Do not create a second homepage merely because an existing report is edited on a later date. If absent, create it using a nearby daily homepage’s conventions without copying its findings.
- Always organize the entire affected homepage after adding or updating a report; do not stop at appending a section. Use a consistent structure: a brief daily overview, a compact report index, then one summarized section per report with selected figures and a link to the full comparison note. Consolidate scattered or overlapping sections while preserving unique findings, material caveats, and source links.
- Read the entire homepage first and find existing mentions of the report by comparison-note link and run/dataset/step identity, including summary tables and figure sections. Update the existing entry in place; add one concise entry only for a new report. A rerun must not append a second copy, and a newly superseding report should refresh the same topic’s current summary while preserving explicitly dated historical conclusions where useful.
- Sort report sections and the report index by report update time, newest first. Show an explicit `Updated: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm PDT/PST` timestamp per report, using `America/Los_Angeles`; distinguish this from the experiment/evidence timestamp. Advance a report’s update time only when its substantive content changes, not when merely reordering or formatting the page. Preserve known timestamps for other reports; when unavailable, label the time unknown and place those entries after dated reports without inventing timestamps.
- Show only the key figures and findings: a compact set of decisive metrics (for example baseline→target WER and error delta), the main improvement/regression pattern, and any limitation that changes the interpretation. Embed only the most informative figure or small selection of figures when available, reusing vault assets; omit redundant plots and do not invent figures or measurements. Link to the comparison note for the full analysis and HTML artifacts. Do not copy the full report, all cases, or all figures onto the homepage.
- Prefer validation `p_err` across training steps as the lead homepage figure when history is available. Show each dataset separately (or in clearly labeled panels), training step on the x-axis, and `p_err` in percent on the y-axis, with labeled runs and lower-is-better interpretation. Reuse the verified trajectory figure, or create it from available verified histories; preserve actual logged steps and gaps without inventing or interpolating observations. Prefer this trajectory over endpoint-only bars or reward plots when choosing the small homepage figure set. If only a single checkpoint or no validation history is available, use the most informative supported figure and state the coverage limit.
- Before delivery, verify note/asset links resolve, metrics agree with the generated summary and reviewed evidence, and the whole affected homepage is structured, summarized with selected available figures, sorted newest-update-first, and free of duplicate report sections or repeated figures. Keep the overview/index concise pointers rather than copies of the report sections. Return links to both the comparison note and daily homepage alongside the HTML reports.

## Scope, consistency, and delivery
- This skill handles writing and organizing existing research evidence. It does not launch training/evaluation or imply permission to commit or push the vault. Follow the calling workflow’s authorization for vault edits. For non-comparison research notes, use the vault’s matching topic folder and template rather than forcing them into the comparison folder.
- Preserve filenames/backlinks, unrelated personal content, managed-report markers, and generator conventions. If renaming is needed, repair backlinks or leave a redirect. Move detailed material out of an overloaded homepage into its linked note without discarding unique evidence.
- Replace stale claims when verified results supersede them; label retained snapshots as historical. Keep validation subsets and full datasets distinct, with sample counts, checkpoint steps, metric units, and provenance. Mark provisional results clearly. Use only figures supported by available evidence; select informative validation, full-dataset, or reward plots as relevant instead of embedding every plot.
- When commit/push is authorized, include only task notes/assets, preserve unrelated dirty/staged/divergent work, and verify the pushed remote SHA. Report the detailed-note and homepage paths, figures updated, and whether changes are local, committed, or pushed.
